Stemwise design

18 · Guided tour

P-020. The tour that starts by itself on the very first launch and again from Help › Take the Tour or from the Welcome screen. It runs on a demo song that the app builds and synthesises itself (PRJ-9): not a project of the user, never saved, gone when the tour ends. Fifteen steps, moved on with Next: a spotlight on the area a step talks about, which stays usable, and a bubble beside it. Every step sets up the state it shows, forwards and backwards. No model is called: the proposal comes from the offline demo, at no cost.

18a

1 · Opening card

On the Welcome screen, as soon as the window is ready on the first launch (the “shown” mark is written now). No lit area: the whole window dims. The demo song is built while this is read, so Start is never a wait; if it is pressed before the song is ready, the next step says so (as in 18p).

Stemwise

Mix and master the songs you have already recorded. An assistant proposes, you listen and decide.

Take the tour· about 3 minutes Drop a folder of stems anywhere on this window to start a project from it.
Set up the assistantOptional

Stemwise asks a language model for mix and master proposals through an OpenRouter account that is yours. Setting it up takes about two minutes; you can also do it later in Settings.

1Connect your OpenRouter accountin the browser
2Add a little credit$5 is plenty to start
3Ask for your first mix
Your audio never leaves this MacThe model receives measurements, roles, track names, your brief and your requests. Never audio, file names, paths or the song title.
Try the offline demoA built-in rule-based assistant that needs no account and no network. Good for a first look.
No recent projects yet.

Welcome to Stemwise

A three-minute tour on a demo song: the mix, the assistant, the master and the export. Nothing you change here is saved, and nothing leaves this Mac.

The demo song is synthesised on this Mac from simple sounds, so it sounds a little plain.

Listening to the proposalSwitch while it plays. Nothing is applied yet. Shortcut B

Vocal forward, guitars opened to the sides, fuller choruses. Drums 1 dB down to make room; bass ducks slightly under the kick.

Distance to target4.8 → 2.1
True peak−3.1 dBTP headroom kept
Loudness−16.4 LUFS no clipping, mono safe
Lead Vox45 changes

Lead vocal sat 2.1 LU under the reference vocal-to-mix balance and was masked by the guitars around 2–4 kHz in the choruses. Raised it 1.8 dB, cut some 220 Hz mud, added presence at 3.2 kHz, and lifted it a further 1.5 dB in the choruses only.

Fader−7.6→−5.8 dB
EQ 1 · 220 Hz0.0→−2.5 dB
EQ 2 · 3.2 kHz0.0→+2.0 dB
Comp threshold−14.0→−18.0 dB
Chorus · fader offset0.0→+1.5 dB
New in this proposal3 of 3 will be created · one undo step removes them with the rest
Vocal plateNewLead Vox sends here
reverb return · plate, 1.1 sA short, bright space for the vocal alone.
SlapNewLead Vox sends here
delay return · 110 ms, no repeatsSlapback: body on the vocal without a tail.
PadsNew2 tracks move into it
group · Rhodes, StringsOne bus to tuck the pads under the vocal together.
Tracks, groups and returns14 of 14 selected
Kick13 changes
Keeps its click at 3 kHz; 1 dB down with the drum group.
Snare4 changes
A little more body at 200 Hz, faster compressor release.
Overheads2 changes
High-pass at 180 Hz so the kick stays clean.
Room3 changes
Down 2 dB and darker: the brief asks for dry drums.
Bass DI24 changes
Ducks 2 dB on every kick through a sidechain.
Acoustic3 changes
Thinned below 120 Hz, panned slightly left.
Gtr Left34 changes
Wide left, 2.5 dB dip at 3 kHz where it masked the vocal.
Gtr Right34 changes
Mirror of Gtr Left on the right side.
Rhodes2 changes
Sent to Echo in the bridge only.
Strings2 changes
Up 1.5 dB in the last chorus.
Drums · group11 changes
Group fader 1 dB down to make room for the vocal.
Plate · reverb4 changes
Shorter and darker; pre-delay 20 ms.
Echo · delay3 changes
Dotted eighth at 375 ms, feedback 25 %.

In short

12 tracks reach the mix bus through 2 groups and share 2 effects. is in front: it is the loudest track, 1.4 LU above . Kick and hold the low end, and the bass steps back each time the kick hits. The guitars are spread to the sides; voice, bass and drums stay in the centre. The choruses are fuller: three more tracks play there and the voice comes up 1.5 dB.

11 tracks set by the assistant1 locked3 changes by hand since

How it is built

2 groups

takes and treats them as one instrument: one EQ, one parallel compressor at 50 %, one fader for all four. takes and shares one EQ.

2 shared effectsreturns

is a plate reverb with a 1.2 s tail: 4 tracks send a copy of themselves to it. is a delay on dotted eighths: 2 tracks send to it. Only the effect comes back into the mix.

5 tracks go straight to the mix bus

Who is in front

loudness of each family
Vocals
−19.8 LUFSDrums
−21.2 LUFSBass
−22.6 LUFSGuitars
−24.9 LUFSKeys and strings
−28.3 LUFSShared effects
−32.0 LUFS

How loud each family is in the mix, over the whole song. The vocals lead by 1.4 LU; keys and strings sit 8.5 LU behind them, as a background.

Left to right

LeftCentreRight

and are far apart (80 % left, 80 % right); is slightly left, slightly right. The other 8 tracks are in the centre.

Space

is the wettest track in (−12 dB), then (−14 dB), (−18 dB) and (−20 dB): the more a track sends, the further back it sounds. Kick, bass and electric guitars send nothing: they stay dry and close.

Who reacts to whom

The compressor of listens to : each kick hit turns the bass down by about 2 dB for a moment, so the two do not pile up in the low end.

What changes along the song

Choruses0:48 · 1:52 · 2:48

play only here. is 1.5 dB louder. is 1.5 dB louder in the last one.

Bridge2:24

sends to only here. Kick and snare stop.

Everything else

8 tracks keep the same settings from start to end.

Reasons

Auto mix · applied 21:44

Vocal forward, guitars opened to the sides, fuller choruses. Drums 1 dB down to make room; bass ducks slightly under the kick.

4
Lead VoxUp 1.8 dB, less mud, more presence; a further 1.5 dB in the choruses.
1
Kick · SnareDrums sit 1 dB lower as a group so the vocal has room; the kick keeps its click at 3 kHz.
2
Bass DIDucks 2 dB on every kick (sidechain) to free the low end without thinning the bass.
3
Gtr Left · RightOpened wide and dipped 2.5 dB at 3 kHz, only where they masked the vocal.

Reasons are the assistant’s own words, kept with each change it made. Changes made by hand have no reason attached.

A three-minute tour on a demo song
18t

App menu › Help › Take the Tour

Every command of Stemwise lives in the app menu, opened from the project name in the top bar (Mix and Master): New project and Open, the project’s own commands, Settings, and the new Help submenu with Take the Tour. The macOS menu bar keeps only what macOS provides (About, Services, Hide, Quit; Edit for text fields; Window). Take the Tour is off while the assistant works, a bounce runs or an export runs (right). With a project open it goes through 18u. On the Welcome screen, where there is no project name, the link of 18s does the same.

Taking the tour with a project open

The tour asks what closing the project asks, with one line about why. Cancel keeps the project and no tour starts; Save or Don’t save close it, and the tour starts on its opening card. At the end the Welcome screen comes back; the project is not reopened.

The demo can’t be prepared

If building the demo song fails (a full disk, an error), the opening card says so instead of Start, the tour ends and the app works as usual. No “shown” mark is lost: the tour can be taken again from Help.

Set up the assistantOptional

Stemwise asks a language model for mix and master proposals through an OpenRouter account that is yours. Setting it up takes about two minutes; you can also do it later in Settings.

1Connect your OpenRouter accountin the browser
2Add a little credit$5 is plenty to start
3Ask for your first mix
Your audio never leaves this MacThe model receives measurements, roles, track names, your brief and your requests. Never audio, file names, paths or the song title.
Try the offline demoA built-in rule-based assistant that needs no account and no network. Good for a first look.
